classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the uniform weekly increase separately for an annual average, unchanged standard deviation and total weekly payroll. This requires routine selection of the translation rule and the appropriate time or employee multiplier.

content.prompt: An employer has 29 employees whose weekly salaries have $\bar{x}=\$429$ and $\sigma=\$1.53$. The employer decides to give a flat $\$100$ raise to every employee.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What would be the change to the average annual salary paid by the employer?

answer.worked:
The average weekly salary increases by $\$100$. Using $52$ weeks in a year, the average annual salary increases by

$$\$100\times52=\$5200.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Would there be a change in the standard deviation?

answer.short: No; the weekly standard deviation remains $\$1.53$.
answer.worked: Every weekly salary and the weekly mean increase by $\$100$. Each deviation from the mean is unchanged, so the weekly standard deviation remains $\$1.53$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What would be the change in total weekly payments to employees?

answer.worked:
Each of the $29$ employees receives an extra $\$100$ per week, so total weekly payments increase by

$$29\times\$100=\$2900.$$
